LEARNING POINTS"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cb\u003EOSCE LEARNING POINTS\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E1. What is PUO?\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;Increase in body temperature more than 38.3 °C (101.0 °F) for at least 21 days or three weeks without any established aetiology (cause) after being a thorough clinical evaluation\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E2.Types of PUO?\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ECLASSICAL PUO: Increase in body temperature for more than 3 weeks and duration of hospital stay is 3 days or 3 outpatient visits without detecting a cause or 1 week of thorough investigations\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENOSOCOMIAL PUO: Temperature of more than 38.3 C developing on several occasions in a\u0026nbsp; Hospitalized patient in whom infection was not manifested or incuabting on admission\u0026nbsp; with 3 days of investigations including atleast 2 days incubation\u0026nbsp; of cultures\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENEUTROPENIC PUO: Temperature of more than 38.3 C developing on several occasions in a patient whose neutrophil count is less than 500\/ microlit or expected to fall in 1-2 days .\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHIV ASSOCIATED PUO:Temperature of more than 38.3 C on several occasions for a period of more than 4 weeks for outpatient or\u0026nbsp; more than 3 days for inpatients\u0026nbsp; with HIV with 3 days of investigations including atleast 2 days incubation\u0026nbsp; of cultures.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E3. Patterns of fever ?\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EContinuous fever : Temperature remains\u0026nbsp; elevated above normal not touching the baseline and fluctuation so not exceed 0.6C\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ERemittent Fever: Temperature fluctuation exceeds more than 0.6 C\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIntermittent Fever : Elevated temperature touches the baseline in between\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ERelapsing fever:Febrile episodes are seperated by normal temperature for more than 1day\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ELEARNING POINTS\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cul\u003E\u003Cli\u003ELearnt how much a fever chart is important\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003EI have learned about patterns of fever\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003ELearnt how much daily routine is important in a patient case\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003ELearnt the importance of patient’s whole history\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003EI learned about importance of timely investigations in thi id=\"post-body-9084838608663899799\"\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis is an\u0026nbsp;an\u0026nbsp;online e log book to discuss our patient de-identified health data shared after taking his \/ her \/ guardians signed informed consent. Here we discuss our individual patients problems through series of inputs from available global online community of experts with an aim to solve those patients clinical problem with collective current best evident based input\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EK.Sri Harshitha\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p2\"\u003EROLL NO:-58\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p2\"\u003EUNIT-I\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p2\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\"\u003EThis E blog also reflects my patient centered online learning portfolio and your valuable inputs on the comment box is welcome.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p2\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003EI have been given this case to solve in an attempt to understand the topic of \" patient clinical data analysis\" to develop my competency in reading and comprehending clinical data including history, clinical findings, investigations and come up with diagnosis and treatment plan\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p2\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003EThe patient\/ attender was informed the purpose of the information being acquired. An informed consent was taken from patient\/ attender and there is omission of information that was requested to be omitted.\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p2\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\"\u003E\u003C\/span\u003ECONSENT WAS GIVEN BY BOTH PATIENT AND ATTENDERS\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"s1\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003ECASE PRESENTATION:-\u003C\/b\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\"\u003EPatient came to the casualty with complaints of fever since 1 month, knee pain since 1 month, cough with sputum since 1 week.\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EHISTORY OF PRESENTING ILLNESS:-\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\"\u003EPatient was apparently asymptomatic 1 month back, then she developed low grade fever- evening rise of temperature, intermittent type , associated with chills.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\"\u003EShe complains of knee joint pains , which is dull aching , non progressive, , no aggravating and relieving factors.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\"\u003ECough With sputum of minimal quantity, white in colour, thin texture.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\"\u003EShe came home for holidays 1 month back.Then after next day of Dusshera she developed fever and weakness for which she went to a local RMP and the RMP told that she has typhoid (no documents) and was given medications( no documents).\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\"\u003EShe was feeling alright for the next 1 week , then again she developed fever for which she again visited the same RMP and this time the RMP told that she has some blood infection (no documents) and was given medication(no documents).\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\"\u003EThis time the fever didn't subside .Then she visited a private hospital and investigations were done, but her complaints were not subsided for which she came to our hospital.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\"\u003ENo h\/o headache, redness of eyes.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\"\u003ENo h\/o dysphagia, dyspnoea, throat pain.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\"\u003ENo h\/o abdominal pain, burning micturition.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\"\u003ENo h\/o bleeding manifestations.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EPAST HISTORY:-\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\"\u003EN\/k\/c\/o. DM, HTN ,epilepsy, thyroid disorders, CAD, CVA.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EPERSONAL HISTORY:-\u003C\/b\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\"\u003EDiet - mixed\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\"\u003EAppetite- decreased\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\"\u003EBowel and bladder- regular\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\"\u003ESleep- adequate\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\"\u003EAddictions- none.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp class=\"p1\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EDAILY
